name: Klebanov-Witten Conifold Throat
description: The throat of threebranes at a conifold singularity: anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times the compact space $T^{1,1}$. Its internal circle twists over two 2-spheres, and a self-dual 5-form flux supports the curvature of the ten dimensions.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit and use the Ricci contraction $R_{\mu\nu}=R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: The compact dimensions of the Klebanov-Witten throat form a circle bundle over two 2-spheres. Igor R. Klebanov and Edward Witten identified the throat of threebranes at a conifold singularity with anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times $T^{1,1}$ in 1998 [klebanovwitten1998]. The anti-de Sitter factor contains time and four spatial dimensions. The remaining five dimensions form the compact space $T^{1,1}$. Philip Candelas and Xenia C. de la Ossa constructed the conifold's Ricci flat Kähler metric in 1990 [candelas1990conifold, klebanovwitten1998].¶Its line element is $ds_6^2=dr^2+r^2ds_{T^{1,1}}^2$, with angular distances proportional to the distance from its tip. The cone has six spatial dimensions and supplies the geometry transverse to the threebranes. Its tip is a curvature singularity, where the compact base shrinks to a point. Larry James Romans had included this compactification among his solutions of chiral supergravity in 1985 [romans1985compactification]. The internal space is the quotient $(SU(2)\times SU(2))/U(1)$, with the circle embedded diagonally in the two factors.¶Its isometries form $SU(2)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$, and the compactification preserves eight supersymmetries [klebanovwitten1998]. Klebanov and Witten proposed that string theory on this throat is dual to a conformal gauge theory in four dimensions [klebanovwitten1998]. The gauge group is $SU(N)\times SU(N)$, where $N$ counts the threebranes. Two pairs of matter fields couple the two gauge groups, and a quartic superpotential preserves the two sphere symmetries. The resulting theory has $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetry, with four ordinary supersymmetries and four conformal partners.¶The two factors share one curvature scale [klebanovwitten1998]. The compact base has positive Einstein curvature, and its normalization makes the cone Ricci flat. In the throat, the 5-form flux supports a nonzero Ricci tensor, with equal and opposite eigenvalues on the two factors. Its scalar curvature vanishes, and its curvature remains finite at the Poincaré horizon. Steven S. Gubser and Klebanov matched D3-branes wrapping 3-cycles of $T^{1,1}$ with baryonlike operators of scaling dimension ($3N/4$) at large $N$ in 1998 [gubserklebanov1998baryons].¶Anna Ceresole and coauthors assembled the Kaluza-Klein spectrum into supersymmetry multiplets in 1999; a massless vector from the harmonic 3-form couples to the conserved baryonic current [ceresole1999spectroscopy]. David Berenstein, Christopher P. Herzog, and Klebanov quantized the collective motion and supersymmetric fluctuations of wrapped D3-branes in 2002, matching the baryon dimension ($3N/4$) and part of the excitation spectrum [berenstein2002spectra]. Yu Nakayama calculated the superconformal index, a signed count of supersymmetric states, from the Kaluza-Klein spectrum in 2006, with wrapped branes omitted in the large $N$ limit [nakayama2006index]. Klebanov and Arvind Murugan localized threebranes on the finite 2-sphere of a resolved conifold in 2007, obtaining a flow from a $T^{1,1}$ throat to a 5-sphere throat with a baryonic condensate [klebanovmurugan2007resolved]. Herzog and coauthors constructed baryonically charged black threebranes in 2010; the zero temperature throat approaches two dimensional anti-de Sitter space times $\mathbb{R}^3\times T^{1,1}$, with logarithmic warp factors [herzog2010baryonic]. Davide Cassani and Anton F. Faedo retained the $SU(2)\times SU(2)$ invariant fields in a consistent reduction to five dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ gauged supergravity with three vector multiplets in 2011 [cassani2011conifold].¶Iosif Bena and coauthors obtained a consistent reduction with the same field content; solutions of the reduced equations lift to solutions in ten dimensions [bena2011truncations]. Pallab Basu and Leopoldo A. Pando Zayas established nonintegrability for a class of classical strings winding around two internal angles in 2011; the winding couples the angular motions through the circle fibration [basu2011nonintegrability]. Mihai Visinescu expressed geodesic motion on $T^{1,1}$ through five independent constants of motion, constant actions, and uniformly advancing angles in 2016 [visinescu2016integrability]. Alex Buchel constructed Euclidean wormholes with two compact hyperbolic boundaries in a mass deformed conifold geometry in 2024, stable against decay through D3-brane and anti-D3-brane nucleation above a critical deformation [buchel2024wormholes]. Buchel constructed black holes with R-charge and scalar or 3-form condensates in 2025; the flux condensate has lower free energy at fixed temperature and chemical potential, and the scalar condensate has higher entropy at fixed energy and charge [buchel2025fluxification]. Oren Bergman and coauthors proposed nonsupersymmetric D4-branes wrapping the internal 2-cycle as operators of the baryonic symmetry in 2025 [bergman2025nonbps].¶Federico Castellani generated marginal and dipole deformations of a twisted circle compactification by T-duality and an angular shift that year; the dipole deformation changes the ultraviolet asymptotics, and both deformations confine boundary quarks [castellani2025tst]. Oscar Henriksson, Niko Jokela, and Julia Junttila calculated nucleation rates and subsonic wall speeds for D5-brane bubbles in the baryonically charged geometry in 2025, using the probe approximation [henriksson2025higgs]. Buchel found a dynamical instability of the baryonically charged black threebranes in 2025; at sufficiently low temperature, fluctuations of the R-charge grow along the horizon [buchel2025baryonic]. Hugo Calvo and coauthors proposed a baryonic symmetry operator formed by a D5-brane and an anti-D5-brane joined into a U shaped configuration that June [calvo2025defects]. Calvo and coauthors proposed nonsupersymmetric Kaluza-Klein monopoles wrapping the $S^2\times S^2$ base as R-symmetry operators later that year, reproducing the mixed anomaly with the baryonic symmetry [calvo2025symmetries]. Ibrahima Bah and coauthors constructed bound states of D5-branes and Kaluza-Klein monopoles that generate continuous isometry symmetries of $T^{1,1}$ in 2026; tachyon condensation controls the fusion of the hanging branes [bah2026measurement].¶Nakayama and Tadashi Okazaki evaluated supersymmetric spectral sums on $T^{1,1}$ in 2026, recovering the integral of squared Riemann curvature and subleading conformal anomalies [nakayama2026spectral]. Pietro Benetti Genolini, Christopher Couzens, and Alice Lüscher used equivariant localization to evaluate supersymmetric D3-brane actions in black hole uplifts on $T^{1,1}$ in 2026 [benetti2026probes]. Alfredo González Lezcano and coauthors quantized a sector of wrapped brane excitations in July 2026 and recovered contributions to the superconformal index [gonzalez2026giants]. Jaehyeok Choi and coauthors constructed infinitely many classical supersymmetry cohomology classes for gauge group $SU(2)\times SU(2)$ and proposed an interpretation with black holes surrounded by baryonic condensates that September [choi2026fortuity]. Antonio Amariti, Riccardo Salto, and Chiara Toldo found marginally stable supersymmetric configurations of wrapped D3-branes outside rotating black holes later that month, within the probe approximation [amariti2026grey]. Evan Deddo and coauthors quantized the scalar, vector, and fermion fluctuations of wrapped D3-branes in October 2026, reproducing the contributions of individual wrapped branes to the index [deddo2026giants].

related.text: Both throats arise from threebranes and pair anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions with a compact space of the same radius. A round 5-sphere preserves 32 supersymmetries, while $T^{1,1}$ preserves eight and has $SU(2)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$ isometry [klebanovwitten1998].

The noncompact factor is anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions, with the same constant negative curvature construction as the geometry of four dimensions. The compact factor is $T^{1,1}$ [klebanovwitten1998].
Both geometries contain a spatial circle fibred over a 2-sphere. The internal circle of the throat has a connection with one contribution from each of two 2-spheres [klebanovwitten1998].
The angular connection in Taub-NUT and the circle fibre of $T^{1,1}$ both twist over a 2-sphere. The throat's fibre is spatial and extends over two spheres [klebanovwitten1998].

coordinates.name: Poincaré

parameters.description: The common curvature length of the anti-de Sitter and compact factors, with $L>0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t,x,y,z,r,\theta,\phi,\alpha,\beta,\psi)$, with $t$ a time, $x$, $y$, $z$, and $r$ lengths, and the remaining coordinates dimensionless angles. The sphere angles are $(\theta,\phi)$ and $(\alpha,\beta)$, corresponding to $(\theta_1,\phi_1)$ and $(\theta_2,\phi_2)$ in the conifold notation, and $\psi$ parametrizes the circle fibre. We take components in the chart $x^0=ct$, with a dot denoting differentiation with respect to an affine parameter $\lambda$.
